instruction: Sort the employee records in the Employee Performance Evaluation Summary spreadsheet alphabetically by employee name (column A) in ascending order (A to Z).

command: import pyautogui; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); import time; time.sleep(1)

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to transfer Excel data to PDF forms. Opened spreadsheet, navigated file system, opened terminal, installed pandas/pdfplumber/openpyxl, and started writing a Python script to fill PDFs. Never completed the PDF generation within 34 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can read spreadsheet data in LibreOffice Calc, navigate file system, open terminal, install Python packages, write Python scripts, interact with cells
metadata.failure_analysis: Original task was too complex: transferring data from Excel to 7 individual PDF forms programmatically. Model spent most turns installing packages and writing scripts, never completing PDF generation.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a data sorting task in LibreOffice Calc, which requires using the Data > Sort menu or similar. Tests model's ability to use Calc features.
metadata.explanation: Task requires sorting rows 2-8 by column A alphabetically. Getter reads employee names from A2:A8 after saving. Metric checks each name position against expected sorted order, giving partial credit per correct position (1/7 each).

scoring_breakdown.per_name: 1/7 each - Each correctly positioned employee name after sorting

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads employee names from cells A2:A8 (column 1, rows 2-8), matching the 7 expected employees
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses expected.get('sorted_names', []) without wrapping
Expected names are verified to be in correct alphabetical order: Alex Lee, David Wilson, Emily Johnson, John Doe, Linda Green, Michael Brown, Sophia Carter
Position-by-position comparison with partial credit (1/7 per correct position) is a sound scoring approach
Postconfig correctly activates the spreadsheet window and saves (Ctrl+S) before getter reads the file, ensuring state freshness
Minor limitation: only verifies column A name order, not that entire rows (other columns) moved together during sort, but this strongly implies correct full-row sorting
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optionally add a second check verifying that at least one other column's data moved consistently with column A (e.g., check that the row for 'Alex Lee' has the correct associated data), to confirm full-row sort rather than column-only sort
